E-commerce / Jewellery & luxury

Live-rate pricing, verified orders and custom pieces on schedule

Jewelry and luxury buyers expect transparency on price and purity, personal attention and care with high-value orders. We automate rate-linked price updates with approval, video consultations, high-value order verification, custom-order tracking through hallmarking, policy-grounded answers on HUID and exchange, and occasion journeys buyers opt into.

The challenge

What makes jewellery & luxury different.

01

Gold prices move daily, so listed prices drift from the metal rate unless someone updates every SKU.

02

Buyers want to verify purity; gold jewelry must carry a BIS hallmark with a six-character HUID in districts where hallmarking is mandatory.

03

High-value orders need verification without asking buyers to share identity documents in chat.

04

Custom pieces pass through designers, karigars and hallmarking centers, and buyers chase updates.

05

Occasion and anniversary moments matter, but only when the buyer chose to share them.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for jewellery & luxury.

01

Rate-linked price updates

Recompute prices from net metal weight, the approved day rate, making charges, stones and tax, hold large moves for approval, and push updates to every channel.

02

Video consultation appointments

Book video or store appointments with a consultant who sees the pieces the buyer saved, and follow up with a written quote.

03

High-value order verification

Hold high-value orders for review, confirm on WhatsApp, and collect any identity or PAN details your policy or tax rules require through a secure form, never in chat.

04

Custom-order tracking through hallmarking

Share milestones from design approval to production, hallmarking and dispatch, with the HUID recorded on the order.

05

Answers on purity, HUID and exchange

Answer questions on hallmarks, HUID verification in the BIS CARE app, and exchange and buyback policy from approved sources, with a consultant on hand.

06

Occasion and lifecycle journeys

Remind buyers of occasions they saved and invite reviews after delivery, with an easy way to remove saved dates.

Automation blueprints

The automations we would start with.

Open each blueprint for its trigger, steps, tools, human checkpoint, data handling, deliverables, and measures.

DiscoverAdvanced5–8 weeks

Stock, price and batch sync across every sales channel

Keep sellable stock, prices and offers consistent across the D2C store, marketplaces and quick-commerce partners. Buffers prevent overselling, near-expiry batches are held back or proposed for markdown, and rate-linked prices such as gold jewelry are recalculated for approval.

FMCG & grocery · Electronics & appliances · Jewellery & luxury

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Stock lives in the warehouse system while each marketplace and quick-commerce partner holds its own count, so popular SKUs oversell and cancellations hurt seller ratings. Prices are uploaded by hand, discounts are announced without a traceable reference price, near-expiry batches ship late, and jewelry prices lag the daily metal rate.

Trigger

A stock movement in the OMS or WMS, a scheduled sync interval, a price or offer change approved in the pricing sheet, or the daily metal rate for jewelry.

How it runs

  • Read sellable stock by location and batch from the OMS or WMS and subtract channel buffers agreed per SKU velocity.
  • Exclude food batches that would reach the shopper with less shelf life than FSSAI's e-commerce advisory asks for, at least 30 percent or 45 days before expiry, and list them in a markdown proposal.
  • For jewelry, recompute prices from net metal weight, the approved day rate, making charges, stone value and tax, and hold any change above the agreed tolerance.
  • Keep a dated price history per SKU so any announced discount can show the prior price the amended E-Commerce Rules call for from January 1, 2027.
  • Push stock and approved prices through channel APIs or partner upload files; for quick-commerce partners that buy on purchase orders, track open POs and listing content instead of pushing stock.
  • Raise mismatches, API failures and oversell risks to the marketplace operations queue.

Human checkpoint

The pricing or marketplace manager approves price changes, markdown proposals and any jewelry price move beyond the tolerance. For jewelry, a named person confirms the day rate before it is used.

Tools

nn8nSSupabasePPythonRRetoolSSlack

Systems it connects

  • Unicommerce, EasyEcom or Increff
  • Shopify storefront
  • Amazon SP-API and Flipkart seller APIs
  • Quick-commerce partner portals
  • Jewelry ERP and a day-rate source such as IBJA

Data & consent

Uses SKU, stock, batch, expiry and price data only, with no shopper personal data. Price history and approvals are retained as evidence behind every announced discount, and only pricing and operations roles can change rules or buffers.

What we deliver

  • Channel stock and buffer rules by SKU class
  • Batch and expiry exclusion logic with markdown proposals
  • Price calculation and prior-price history store
  • Exception queue for mismatches and API failures

How we measure it

  • Orders canceled for stock-outs
  • Stock mismatches per channel
  • Near-expiry units sold before cut-off
  • Price change lead time
  • Sync failure rate

EvaluateStandard3–5 weeks

Video and showroom consultation booking

Let shoppers book a video call or showroom visit with a designer or jewelry consultant, pass the right product context to the consultant beforehand, and send follow-ups, quotes and approved financing information after the call.

Home & furniture · Jewellery & luxury

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

High-value furniture and jewelry purchases need conversation, but inquiries arrive across Instagram, WhatsApp and calls and are answered late or lost. Consultants join calls without knowing what the shopper viewed, trade and interior-designer leads mix with retail ones, and EMI questions get improvised answers.

Trigger

A shopper clicks book a consultation on a product or collection page, replies to a click-to-WhatsApp ad, or submits a designer or trade inquiry form.

How it runs

  • Offer open slots by consultant, language, store and category, and confirm by WhatsApp and calendar invite with a reschedule link.
  • Attach the shopper's viewed products, wishlist, budget band and room or occasion notes to the consultant's brief.
  • Route architects, interior designers and bulk buyers to the trade team with their own follow-up rules.
  • Send a reminder before the call and a follow-up afterward with the shortlisted designs or quote.
  • Answer EMI questions only with the current lender-approved terms text, and send the shopper to the lender or payment page for eligibility.
  • Record outcomes such as quote sent, custom order or no sale in the CRM for follow-up.

Human checkpoint

Consultants own every quote, custom-design commitment and price exception. Financing eligibility is decided only by the lender, never by the automation.

Checkout and confirmStandard3–5 weeks

COD confirmation, address checks and high-value verification

Confirm cash-on-delivery orders on WhatsApp before dispatch, fix incomplete addresses, and hold risky or high-value orders for a person to review, so fewer parcels travel to doorsteps that will refuse them.

Fashion & apparel · Electronics & appliances · Jewellery & luxury

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Cash on delivery stays popular, and some COD orders are refused at the door, unreachable or placed with incomplete addresses. Each return to origin pays freight both ways and ties up stock; for fashion it often misses the season. Electronics and jewelry add fraud risk: high-value orders with mismatched details.

Trigger

A new order arrives in the storefront or OMS with COD payment, an address that fails validation, or a value above the high-value threshold.

How it runs

  • Validate the address against the pincode serviceability master, flag missing house numbers or landmarks, and score risk from value, order history, pincode return history and past refusals.
  • Send an approved WhatsApp utility template to shoppers who opted in to order updates at checkout, asking them to confirm the order and address, with buttons to confirm, edit the address or cancel.
  • Where the client chooses, add an optional prepaid link. Any COD fee or prepaid benefit is shown at checkout, never added later, and no promotional incentive goes into the utility template.
  • If WhatsApp is undelivered or the shopper has no WhatsApp opt-in, use a DLT-registered SMS service template or an IVR call, then hold the order for review.
  • Queue high-risk and high-value orders with the evidence; for jewelry, collect any identity or PAN details the client's policy requires through a secure web form, not in chat.
  • Release confirmed orders to the warehouse and log outcomes for return-to-origin analysis by pincode, channel and campaign.

Human checkpoint

An order-operations reviewer decides every held or high-value order: release, call the shopper or cancel. Cancellations the shopper asks for are processed as requested; the automation never cancels an order on its own.

Tools

  • Shiprocket, Delhivery or another courier aggregator
  • Pincode serviceability master

Data & consent

Uses order, address, phone and delivery history. Risk rules use order and delivery signals only, never religion, caste, gender or similar traits, and are reviewed for unfair effects on particular pincodes. Identity details are collected only where required, stored encrypted with restricted access and deleted after the retention period.

What we deliver

  • Address validation and risk-scoring rules
  • WhatsApp confirmation templates with SMS and IVR fallbacks
  • Review queue for held and high-value orders
  • Return-to-origin dashboard by pincode, channel and campaign

How we measure it

  • COD confirmation rate before dispatch
  • Return-to-origin rate by payment mode and pincode
  • Address corrections captured
  • Held orders reviewed within SLA

DeliverStandard3–5 weeks

Custom and made-to-order progress tracking

Give custom jewelry and made-to-order furniture buyers a clear timeline, from design approval through production, quality checks and hallmarking where it applies, to delivery, with proactive updates whenever a date moves.

Jewellery & luxury · Home & furniture

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Custom pieces take weeks and pass through designers, karigars or workshops, quality checks and, for gold, a hallmarking center. Buyers chase updates on WhatsApp, staff chase the workshop, and approvals for design changes or extra charges get lost in chat threads.

Trigger

A custom or made-to-order item is confirmed with an advance payment, or the workshop updates a production milestone.

How it runs

  • Create the order record with the approved design, specifications, metal or material, size, price basis and promised date.
  • Send the design proof for the buyer's explicit approval and store the approved version.
  • Let the workshop update milestones such as material issued, in production, quality check, hallmarking and ready to ship from a simple mobile form.
  • Send an update at each milestone and alert the store team when a milestone slips past its planned date.
  • Request written approval for any change to design, weight-based price or delivery date before work continues.
  • Hand over to delivery with the HUID or material certificate recorded on the order where applicable.

Human checkpoint

The store manager or designer agrees design changes, revised quotes and new dates with the buyer. The quality team signs off every piece before dispatch.

Returns and supportAdvanced5–8 weeks

Policy-grounded support assistant with human handoff

Answer order, policy, product-care and service questions on WhatsApp and web chat from the store's own policies and live order data, raise service and quality tickets with the right details, and hand over to an agent whenever a question needs judgment.

FMCG & grocery · Electronics & appliances · Jewellery & luxury

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Support teams answer the same questions all day: where is my order, can I cancel, how do I use this, is this piece hallmarked, how do I claim warranty. Sale days overwhelm them and answers drift from the published policy. A bot that improvises refund or warranty terms creates disputes.

Trigger

A shopper messages the brand on WhatsApp, web chat or email.

How it runs

  • Identify the shopper and order from the WhatsApp number or order ID, with a one-time code on web chat and email before sharing order details.
  • Answer only from approved sources: return, cancellation, warranty and exchange policies, care guides, hallmark and HUID verification guidance, and live order status.
  • For electronics, open a service ticket with model, serial number, purchase date and symptoms, and explain the visit or pickup process.
  • For FMCG and grocery, capture the batch number and photos for quality or expiry complaints and route them to the quality team.
  • Hand over to an agent with a summary when the shopper asks, confidence is low, or the topic is a refund dispute, safety issue, legal complaint or anything the policy does not cover.
  • Acknowledge complaints within the grievance timelines the client publishes and track each to closure.

Human checkpoint

Agents own refunds, compensation, safety and quality complaints and every policy exception; the grievance officer handles escalated complaints. A QA reviewer samples conversations every week.

Repeat and advocateStandard4–6 weeks

Reviews, drops, back-in-stock and lifecycle journeys

Use RFM segments and stated preferences to send the few messages shoppers value: review and photo requests after delivery, back-in-stock and new-drop alerts they signed up for, and reminders for occasions they chose to share, with reviews published unedited.

Fashion & apparel · Beauty & personal care · Jewellery & luxury

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Brands blast the whole list with every sale, which raises opt-outs and hurts WhatsApp quality ratings. Review requests go out before the parcel arrives or only to happy customers, back-in-stock sign-ups are never notified, and jewelry buyers who shared an anniversary date hear nothing until the next sale.

Trigger

Delivery is confirmed, a sold-out size or shade returns to stock, a new collection goes live, a segment changes, or a saved occasion date approaches.

How it runs

  • Build RFM and preference segments in the warehouse from orders, returns and stated preferences such as size, shade or metal.
  • Request a review and photo from every buyer a set time after delivery, not only satisfied ones, and publish reviews without changing their meaning.
  • Notify back-in-stock sign-ups in sign-up order when the exact size or shade returns.
  • Send new-drop previews to opted-in segments with the real stock position and no fake scarcity.
  • Send occasion reminders only to buyers who saved the date for that purpose, with an easy way to remove it.
  • Measure each journey against a holdout and retire messages that do not earn their place.

Human checkpoint

The CRM manager approves segments, frequency caps and copy. A moderator reviews flagged reviews under a published moderation policy, guided by the voluntary BIS standard IS 19000:2022, and never removes a review for being negative.
